status: Proposed study; primary images remain current VN assets, unedited

references.title: Home: an enclosed, personal place
references.story: revision/latest.md:61–77; branching halls and private rooms
references.observed: A central table, books and drawings, close seating, a small fountain and several arched thresholds. The room feels occupied and sheltered.
references.proposal: Embed domestic rooms in thick living structure, with nearby courts and private thresholds. Keep the furnished room at human scale.
references.unknown: The number of homes beyond the doors, the pressure boundary and the ship-wide dwelling pattern are not visible.

pins.text: Table, books and work in progress establish everyday occupation.
Successive arches make enclosure and connections tangible.
A planted view beyond a threshold; not proof of a planet-like exterior.

references.title: Courtyard: social life among cultivated structure
references.story: revision/latest.md:57; connected paths, gardens and plazas
references.observed: A low shared table is surrounded by intimate seating, planted edges and curved adjoining passages. Light is filtered through canopy.
references.proposal: Use many small neighborhood courts, with varied public/private edges, inside the larger connected anatomy.
references.unknown: This frame does not establish that every court has the same plan, or that all residents share this one court.

pins.text: Seated people and the table establish a small social scale.
A curved passage carries the scene beyond its immediate gathering space.
Canopy and planted overhead connections create filtered enclosure.

references.title: Garden and oak: two related inhabited heights
references.runtime: bg garden · visuals.rpy:12 · script.rpy:177; treehouse entrance sequence
references.story: revision/latest.md: treehouse chapters; oak, ladder and separate lower hollow
references.observed: The upper room sits among the oak branches. A ladder meets its right-hand entrance; a separate lower hollow and broad seating refuge occupy the bank below.
references.proposal: Give the oak genuine rooting depth and canopy clearance within a garden terrace. Preserve the distinct upper entrance, ladder and lower refuge.
references.unknown: This oak is not the Tree of Echoes. Its visible scale does not determine the material or size of Lumen’s main structural supports.

pins.text: Upper room: handmade, inhabited and sheltered by branches.
The ladder connects to the upper entrance; the lower hollow is separate.
A broad refuge sits at garden level. Root and drainage volume must fit beneath it.

references.title: Treehouse interior: intimacy survives verticality
references.runtime: bg treehouse · visuals.rpy:17 · script.rpy:187; actor staging in visuals.rpy:24–28
references.story: revision/latest.md: patchwork treehouse, open cutouts and curtains
references.observed: The oak crosses the room. The roof is low, the bays open to foliage, and curtains, cushions, drawings and a map table make a personal refuge.
references.proposal: Reconstruct the room, door, landing and canopy as one local space before placing it in the world. Preserve the supported floor and open edge.
references.unknown: Its camera and furniture are guides, not a calibrated orthographic drawing; far views do not prove an unobstructed ship-wide sky.

pins.text: The diagonal oak is part of this room’s geometry.
Arched doorway and nearby floor must connect to the exterior landing.
Open bays, rails and curtains preserve the outdoor refuge experience.

references.title: Pond action CG: small geometry carries the story
references.runtime: cg pond_rescue · visuals.rpy:6 · family_book_one.rpy:444; bg garden_pond at :439
references.observed: The rescuers kneel on a broad dry bank beside very low stone coping. The small planted pond, child and reaching hands define the action.
references.proposal: Keep the bank reachable and the pond local to the garden. Reconcile this action framing with the garden-pond background in the local model.
references.unknown: The CG does not calibrate exact water depth. It does not justify converting the pond to a deep reservoir, canal or exposed drop.

pins.text: Hands and low bank make the rescue physically readable.
A small basin supports the scene; exact depth requires comparison with the background.
Dry standing/kneeling room and familiar access are part of the place.

references.title: Construction path: living structure and work coexist
references.story: revision/latest.md:431; machinery, metal, welding and scaffolds
references.observed: Thick branching supports frame a bending path. The left opens onto another occupied height. Scaffolds, boards, rope and tools occupy the foreground.
references.proposal: Let growth fronts attach to existing neighborhoods. Retain unfinished work, material staging and routes passing through thick structure.
references.unknown: The painted supports’ wood-like appearance does not identify the load-bearing material throughout the vessel.

pins.text: Branching support frames a view across a separate inhabited height.
The path turns through structure into further occupied space.
Scaffolding and fabricated pieces are visible parts of construction.

references.title: Construction room: technology remains usable
references.story: revision/latest.md: construction exploration; tools, metal and machinery
references.observed: A furnished workroom contains mechanisms, tools, components and a projected design. An arched side door connects directly to the grown passage.
references.proposal: Embed usable workshops and staging rooms within growth areas. Physical tools and interfaces work alongside advanced systems.
references.unknown: The projected design is not a ship plan, a canon gravity mechanism or proof that every wall can instantly transform.

pins.text: Mechanisms and tools allow real making, inspection and repair.
A visible technical interface; its depicted design does not define Lumen’s anatomy.
The workroom joins the same tangible passage network.

references.title: Dome overlook: the principal reference for connected depth
references.story: revision/latest.md:447–453; local unfinished dome and scaffold ascent
references.observed: An internal stone parapet and scaffolds overlook overlapping gardens, paths, rooms and inhabited terraces at many heights. Large grown supports continue beyond the view.
references.proposal: Use branching inhabited structure and multiple connected view volumes. The local overlook reveals a wider pattern without displaying the whole ship.
references.unknown: No exterior silhouette, exact span, total population, roof type or single global ground plane can be measured from this image.

pins.text: Foreground platform and scaffold establish the local ascent viewpoint.
Many occupied heights overlap through depth; this is the central spatial relationship to preserve.
Rooms, foliage and supports continue beyond the immediate opening.

references.title: Festival: a social focus with occupied galleries
references.observed: An intimate performance platform, a curved stair at left, occupied upper galleries and a rear passage support a crowded gathering under lanterns.
references.proposal: Treat the named central plaza as a connected civic place with real approaches and multiple occupied heights, within a distributed world.
references.unknown: Visible galleries do not establish total gathering capacity. Keep the manuscript’s whole-community claim open for a measured test; do not infer a census from painted heads.

pins.text: Small stage and nearby listeners give the event its intimate scale.
People occupy upper galleries as well as the court.
A rear passage continues beyond the foreground gathering; its capacity is unknown.

references.title: Tree of Echoes: a distinct heritage grove
references.story: revision/latest.md: Tree of Echoes passage; wiki/worldbuilding/Lumen.md
references.observed: A single gnarled hollow tree stands in a deeply enclosed, shaded grove with trailing vegetation and cool local light. No treehouse is visible.
references.proposal: Place this as a quieter, distinct place within the garden network. Give its tree a credible root zone; preserve its role in Lumen’s gradual revelation.
references.unknown: The tree is not evidence for a sole ship-wide trunk, a central brain or the oak treehouse’s location.

pins.text: The hollow heritage tree remains distinct from the children’s oak.
Layered canopy and enclosure make a sheltered, reflective place.
Small local light sources shape mood; they do not establish the crop-energy supply.
